text:
Mia: Post-RFC follow-up: we need concrete guardrails around claim pruning + RBAC enforcement. Concern is services doing authz using pruned tokens and returning over-permissive responses.

Kevin: Good call. Two quick options: 1) require an unpruned project_id for any route that enforces RBAC locally, or 2) allow compact tokens but force an assertion that service must call authz-service to resolve principal -> roles.

Arya: Option 2 is more flexible but risky for latency. Suggest a hybrid: compact tokens carry project_hash + short role_vector (bitmask) for fast-path checks. If role_vector missing or insufficient, fall back to remote authz.

Noah: Role_vector adds token size but far less than full claims. We can define canonical role bits: read:1, write:2, admin:4, deploy:8. Services can bitwise-check.

Liam: Security ops: role_vector in token must be signed by authn-service and have ttl <= token ttl. Also need CI gating so no service releases with local-RBAC route expecting full claims unless migration flag enabled.

Mia: I like that. For rollback safety, require two toggles: SERVICE_AUTH_PRUNE=(none|compact|hashed) and SERVICE_RBAC_MODE=(local|hybrid|remote). Default internal routes: compact + hybrid.

Arya: Sample route config idea (in service-config.yaml):
```yaml
routes:
  - path: /v1/data
    auth_prune: compact
    rbac_mode: hybrid
    required_roles: [read,write]
```

Kevin: And a runtime assert in dev: if auth_prune != none and rbac_mode == local -> fail startup. This prevents accidental local enforcement without full claims.

Noah: Telemetry: auth.rbac.checks.total, auth.rbac.local.failures, auth.rbac.remote.latency.p95. Also emit token.size.bytes for sampling. We'll run perf tests with role_vector vs full claims.

Liam: Ops: add a CI lint rule in the policy repo that scans service-config.yaml and rejects PRs that set rbac_mode: local if auth_prune != none. ci-bot can enforce.

ci-bot: Note: added pre-merge check in ci pipeline to run policy-lint v1.2 on changed configs.

Mia: Auditability: compact tokens must include audit_ref which maps to the full claim set in authn's audit store for 7 days. That gives oncall breadcrumbs without putting verbose metadata in every token.

Arya: Implementation sketch for SDK: expose function require_roles(request, roles) which internally does: 1) if role_vector present, check locally, 2) else call authz.resolve_principal(audit_ref) and enforce. This centralizes fallback logic.

Kevin: Also add a debug endpoint in authn-service: /introspect?audit_ref=XYZ, returns JSON for ops only. Rate-limit and auth.

Liam: KMS note: hashed project_hash/origin uses rotating key; rotate monthly and record rotation windows in audit store. Security-bot: will open KMS ticket.

Mia: Migration plan bullets:
- Phase 0: Add enums and SDK helpers, CI policy-lint.
- Phase 1: Canary compact+hybrid on low-risk services (metrics + error budget)
- Phase 2: Expand, add audit store retention + perf baseline
- Phase 3: Rollback guard: enforce rbac_mode dev assert and CI lint for 2 weeks post-expand.

Noah: Perf experiment checklist: measure KV cache hit rate, runtime mem, authz.remote.calls per minute. Baseline -> compact w/role_vector -> compact w/o role_vector.

Arya: Edge: third-party webhooks that proxy through internal services must always present full token (auth_prune=none). We'll add route-level allowlist for external origins.

Mia: OK next steps: Arya to prototype role_vector encoding and SDK helpers, Kevin to add CI lint rule, Liam to open KMS ticket and retention policy, Noah to draft perf test plan.

ops-bot: reminder set: follow-up sync in #eng-security on 3133345739 (15m).

Mia: Thanks everyone. If we get prototypes by EOD Friday we can schedule canary next week. :rocket:
